title: Kapranov–Schechtman's total-positivity conjecture for finite Coxeter groups
source: Zhentao Wang, Jiawen Xie and Xuhang Zhang, “On the Total Positivity of Contingency Metamatrices”, arXiv:2503.02213 (2025), Conjecture 1.0.1. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02213

significance.root_decision: The conjecture fails for the Coxeter group of type D_27: the 16×16 submatrix of M(D_27) with rows p = 0..15 and columns q = 12..27 has negative determinant (a 372-digit integer), so M(D_27) is not totally positive, not even totally nonnegative. The source proves the conjecture for type B and the exceptional types and does no type-D computation; every rank from 2 to 26 is totally positive (reproduced independently by two lanes, not formalized and not claimed), so no small-rank check finds the failure. The proof identifies parabolic subgroups with stabilizers of face vectors, counts double cosets by Burnside's lemma through fixed-face counts with a type-D gluing identity (Stembridge's fixed-face data are the closest prior work), and turns the result into an explicit integer formula for every entry. Lean works with the concrete group of even signed permutations of 27 coordinates and its 27 standard reflections (the D_27 fork), defines parabolics as generated subgroups and entries as Nat.card of Mathlib's double-coset quotient, proves the formula, evaluates all 256 entries of the minor in the kernel (decide +kernel, no native_decide), and certifies the sign of the determinant by an integer triangular factorization.
significance.caveat: One cited bridge: Lean proves the statement for the concrete pair (even signed permutations of 27 coordinates, 27 standard reflections) and proves the generators are distinct involutions that generate the group; that this pair is the Coxeter system of type D_27 is the textbook theorem (Bourbaki VI §4.8, Björner–Brenti §8.2), not formalized (the final check verified the analogous pairs for n = 2..5 by computer). The source does not define total positivity; the strict sense used is Kapranov–Schechtman's (Etingof's appendix), and the negative minor also refutes total nonnegativity. Borderline significance: once one decides to compute type D in closed form the method (Stembridge's fixed-face data plus Burnside) is standard; cross-model reviewer not routine 0.55, final checker 0.55–0.60. That rank 27 is the first failure is not formalized and not claimed. The Lean was started by a GPT-6.1 Sol lane and finished by a Claude Opus 5.5 lane (3,942 lines in 39 modules); because GPT-6.1 Sol hit its usage limit, the final check was by a separate Claude Opus 5.5 lane, the same model family as the packager (the cross-model review is the Opus pre-Lean review of a Sol proof).

root_basis: Root (Claude Opus 5.5) extracted the 39 modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three for both endpoints, no forbidden tokens), and compared the final theorem and the definitions of SignedPerm, EvenSignedPerm, simpleD27, parabolic, doubleCount, metamatrix, TotallyPositive, minorRows and minorCols with endpoint E2 written by the Claude Opus referee: identical.
